suite: Zetaris live real-world haze use cases

datasets.NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires: NASA FIRMS VIIRS active fire detections, Malaysia (live fetch)
datasets.air_quality.hourly_observations: Open-Meteo modelled hourly PM2.5/PM10 for 345 Malaysian locations

cases.title: Hotspot inventory: how many active fires were ingested?
cases.why_it_matters: An analyst opening the haze console first needs to know the size and recency of the fire dataset.
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hotspots, MIN(acq_date) AS earliest, MAX(acq_date) AS latest, COUNT(DISTINCT source) AS satellites FROM NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires

cases.title: Which fires are burning hardest? (top fire radiative power)
cases.why_it_matters: Attribution starts from the most energetic fires, because weak detections rarely drive a haze episode.
cases.sql: SELECT location_id, region, ROUND(CAST(frp AS DOUBLE), 2) AS frp_mw, confidence, acq_myt FROM NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires ORDER BY CAST(frp AS DOUBLE) DESC LIMIT 5

cases.title: Detection provenance: which satellite saw what, and when?
cases.why_it_matters: Every claim must name its sensor. Mixed VIIRS platforms must stay distinguishable.
cases.sql: SELECT source, daynight, COUNT(*) AS detections FROM NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires GROUP BY source, daynight ORDER BY detections DESC

cases.title: Geographic spread: where are the fires concentrated?
cases.why_it_matters: Peninsular vs East Malaysia matters: transboundary haze and local burning need different responses.
cases.sql: SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS hotspots, COUNT(DISTINCT location_id) AS locations FROM NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires GROUP BY region ORDER BY hotspots DESC

cases.title: Data-quality gate: confidence distribution of detections
cases.why_it_matters: Low-confidence detections must be separable so they can be excluded from a published finding.
cases.sql: SELECT confidence, COUNT(*) AS detections, ROUND(AVG(CAST(frp AS DOUBLE)), 2) AS mean_frp FROM NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires GROUP BY confidence ORDER BY detections DESC

cases.title: PM2.5 coverage: how much air-quality evidence is retained?
cases.why_it_matters: The modelled PM2.5 feed is the measurement side of the question; its coverage bounds any claim.
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS samples, COUNT(DISTINCT location_name) AS locations, MIN(observation_time) AS first_hour, MAX(observation_time) AS last_hour FROM air_quality.hourly_observations

cases.title: Where is the air worst right now? (peak PM2.5 by location)
cases.why_it_matters: The operational question a resident asks: which places are above the unhealthy threshold?
cases.sql: SELECT location_name, ROUND(MAX(pm2_5_ug_m3), 1) AS peak_pm25, ROUND(AVG(pm2_5_ug_m3), 1) AS mean_pm25 FROM air_quality.hourly_observations GROUP BY location_name ORDER BY peak_pm25 DESC LIMIT 5

cases.title: WHO exceedance: hours above the 15 ug/m3 24-hour guideline
cases.why_it_matters: A policy-relevant count, not a raw reading: how many location-hours breach the WHO 2021 guideline?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS exceeding_hours, COUNT(DISTINCT location_name) AS affected_locations, ROUND(MAX(pm2_5_ug_m3), 1) AS worst FROM air_quality.hourly_observations WHERE pm2_5_ug_m3 > 15

cases.title: CROSS-SOURCE ATTRIBUTION: fires within ~50km of the worst-affected places
cases.why_it_matters: The actual haze-attribution join. Pairs each high-PM2.5 location with nearby active fires, which is what a source-attribution answer must be built on. A crude degree box stands in for a proper geodesic buffer.
cases.sql:
SELECT aq.location_name,
       ROUND(MAX(aq.pm2_5_ug_m3), 1) AS peak_pm25,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.location_id) AS nearby_fire_sites,
       ROUND(SUM(CAST(f.frp AS DOUBLE)), 1) AS nearby_total_frp
FROM air_quality.hourly_observations aq
JOIN NASA_FIRMS_FILES.active_fires f
  ON ABS(CAST(f.latitude AS DOUBLE) - aq.requested_latitude) < 0.45
 AND ABS(CAST(f.longitude AS DOUBLE) - aq.requested_longitude) < 0.45
GROUP BY aq.location_name
ORDER BY nearby_total_frp DESC
LIMIT 8
cases.interpretation_note: A zero-row result is a legitimate finding: it means no ingested fire sits near a monitored location in this window, so no fire-based attribution is supportable from this evidence.

cases.title: Registration metadata is inspectable (schema introspection)
cases.why_it_matters: An auditor must be able to see the registered shape of each source, not just its rows.
